name: Adriano Santos
headline: 48, retired percussionist and theater technician, Rio de Janeiro
title: Sunday Samba Invitation
situation: On a Friday afternoon, Adriano is in his garage re-skinning a floor tom when his neighbor Maria appears at the open door. A samba circle meets every Sunday in the courtyard of the local community center, organized by the residents' association. Maria says the group has an old surdo drum that's been wobbling, and she remembers Adriano's hands. She asks if he'd come by this Sunday, maybe with his tools, to help tune it. He's not asked to play, just to lend his skill. The courtyard will be full of familiar faces from his childhood. He can say yes and spend a few hours helping, or he can make an excuse about his hearing and stay in his garage.

context.relationship_profiles: Maria is his neighbor of ten years, the only one who still stops to talk rather than just wave from behind her gate. She has never asked him for anything before, and he has no particular debt or grudge with her. He knows she is kind but also that she volunteers with the residents' association, which he quietly distrusts.
context.tendencies: When neighbors ask him directly for a small, concrete repair, he has usually said yes—he fixed a broken clothesline for the widow next door and re-glued a chair leg for the corner baker. But he has repeatedly turned down invitations from organized groups, including the residents' association's annual cleanup and a local arts collective's fundraiser. His pattern is to help individuals, not institutions.
context.current_state: He is mid-repair, with drumhead glue still drying on his fingers and a half-tensioned floor tom clamped to the bench. His left ear is ringing slightly from the humid afternoon, and he is a little tired from crouching over the shell. He is calm but guarded, expecting the invitation to carry an obligation he does not want.
context.immediate_memories: When Maria mentions the surdo's wobble, he remembers the last surdo he worked on—a broken bearing edge from a local bloco that he fixed two years ago. Seeing her at the garage door also brings back the Sunday afternoons of his childhood, when he would sit on the curb and watch the samba circle form, listening through the open windows of his father's house.
context.reflective_memories: He recalls the time the residents' association asked him to perform at a holiday event, then spent more time on speeches than letting him set up the drums. He remembers telling his sister that the only honest music happens when no one is trying to organize it. He also remembers that his father, before he died, used to say the community center's courtyard was the one place where everyone was equal—until the association put up metal chairs.
